lines.trans: I swear, I don't know where your elephant is.
I had an epiphany today.
I suddenly realized that you are everything I need.
Let's start everything from a clean slate. Just you and me.
And what next?
Next I will get on my feet, we will get married in about two years.
Then we will have kids in five or six years.
In five or six?
If you want, we can wait even longer. We'll live for ourselves, grow old together, and die on the same day.
And if you want, I can die first! Well, do you like my plan?
It is a good plan, Max.
Only that is your plan, not ours.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'swear', paired with 'поклясться'.

Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will grow old'.

related.gloss: not to will grow old (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и состариться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and will grow old on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют состариться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to will grow old.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'together', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Хочешь, можем ещё подождать. Поживём для себя, состаримся вместе и умрём в один день.
examples.trans: If you want, we can wait even longer. We'll live for ourselves, grow old together, and die on the same day.

examples.text: Мы вместе.
examples.trans: We're together.

examples.text: Мы живём вместе.
examples.trans: We live together.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'мереть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will die', paired with 'умирать'.

examples.text: И хочешь, я могу умереть первый! Ну что, нравится тебе мой план?
examples.trans: And if you want, I can die first! Well, do you like my plan?

examples.text: Она умерла в прошлом году.
examples.trans: She died last year.

examples.text: Он умер очень старым.
examples.trans: He died very old.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никто не раздражает поваров больше, чем официанты.
examples.trans: Nobody irritates cooks more than waiters.

examples.text: Нетерпеливый! Девушки просят меня быть помедленнее.
examples.trans: Impatient! Girls ask me to go more slowly.

examples.text: Давай быстрее готовь!
examples.trans: Come on, cook faster!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: О, грибы! Мне один дурак на корпоративе дал.
examples.trans: Oh, mushrooms! Some fool gave them to me at an office party.

examples.text: Похоже, не ты один пришёл праздновать развод.
examples.trans: It looks like you are not the only one who came to celebrate the divorce.

examples.text: Ты некрасивый. Поди сюда.
examples.trans: You are unattractive. Come here.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'day' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Открытый чемпионат кухни по сбиванию банок. Солидные деньги на кону.
examples.trans: The open kitchen can-knocking championship. Serious money is at stake.

examples.text: И это солидные деньги? Марш работать!
examples.trans: And that is serious money? March back to work!

examples.text: Продолжим удачный день!
examples.trans: Let's continue this lucky day!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('first').

examples.text: И хочешь, я могу умереть первый! Ну что, нравится тебе мой план?
examples.trans: And if you want, I can die first! Well, do you like my plan?

examples.text: Это мой первый день.
examples.trans: This is my first day.

examples.text: Ты не понимаешь с первого раза?
examples.trans: You don't understand the first time?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну, позволю!
examples.trans: Well, I will allow it!

examples.text: Открытый чемпионат кухни по сбиванию банок. Солидные деньги на кону.
examples.trans: The open kitchen can-knocking championship. Serious money is at stake.

examples.text: Ну, что делать? Другой раз, так другой раз.
examples.trans: Well, what can we do? Another time, then another time.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'pleases', paired with 'понравиться'.

examples.text: Мне нравится кофе.
examples.trans: I like coffee.

examples.text: Людям нравится.
examples.trans: People like it.

examples.text: Реакция положительная. Людям нравится.
examples.trans: The reaction is positive. People like it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Всем шампанского за мой счёт!
examples.trans: Champagne for everyone on my tab!

examples.text: Дима, тебе бы поехать домой.
examples.trans: Dima, you should go home.

examples.text: А где мой завтрак? Вот мой завтрак!
examples.trans: And where is my breakfast? Here is my breakfast!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'plan' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы с тобой идём в кино, ничего не планируй.
examples.trans: You and I are going to the cinema, don't plan anything.

examples.text: Дима, а можешь по такому радостному случаю поднять зарплату?
examples.trans: Dima, on such a joyful occasion can you raise my salary?

examples.text: И хочешь, я могу умереть первый! Ну что, нравится тебе мой план?
examples.trans: And if you want, I can die first! Well, do you like my plan?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good').

examples.text: Ребята! Здравствуйте! Ты моя хорошая.
examples.trans: Guys! Hello! You are my good girl.

examples.text: Господа, всем шампанского хорошего!
examples.trans: Ladies and gentlemen, good champagne for everyone!

examples.text: Всем хорошего шампанского!
examples.trans: Good champagne for everyone!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Будешь себя отлично чувствовать.
examples.trans: You will feel great.

examples.text: Не твоё дело. Интересно? К любовнику.
examples.trans: None of your business. Curious? To my lover.

examples.text: Какое твоё собачье дело?
examples.trans: What business is it of yours?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А, всё, нашла.
examples.trans: Ah, that's it, I found it.

examples.text: А насчёт нашего последнего разговора...
examples.trans: And regarding our last conversation...

examples.text: Только это твой план, не наш.
examples.trans: Only that is your plan, not ours.
